steps.say: Lupus nephritis affects forty to sixty percent of SLE patients. Renal biopsy is mandatory for any patient with unexplained persistent proteinuria at or above zero point five grams per twenty four hours or matching spot ratio, or active urinary sediment with dysmorphic hematuria or cellular casts. Protein plus sediment is the needle rule.
steps.tx: **Lupus nephritis** affects **40% to 60%** of SLE patients. Renal **biopsy** is mandatory for any patient with unexplained persistent **proteinuria >=0.5 g/24 hours** (or spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio >=0.5 mg/mg) or active urinary sediment with **dysmorphic hematuria** or **cellular casts**. Protein plus sediment is the needle rule.

steps.say: The ISN RPS histological classification stratifies lupus nephritis into six classes: minimal mesangial Class one, mesangial proliferative Class two, focal proliferative Class three under fifty percent, diffuse proliferative Class four at fifty percent or more, membranous Class five, and advanced sclerosing Class six with ninety percent or more scarred. Class assignment decides the guns.
steps.tx: The **ISN/RPS** histological classification stratifies lupus nephritis into **six classes**: **Class I** (minimal mesangial), Class II (mesangial proliferative), **Class III** (focal proliferative, involving **<50%** of glomeruli), **Class IV** (diffuse proliferative, involving **>=50%** of glomeruli), **Class V** (membranous), and **Class VI** (advanced sclerosing, **>=90%** globally sclerosed glomeruli). Class decides guns.

rows: Advanced sclerosing, 90 percent or more scarred

steps.say: Immunofluorescence microscopy of lupus nephritis characteristically reveals the full-house pattern: dense granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q in mesangium and capillary loops, accompanied by prominent subendothelial immune complex deposits forming wire-loop lesions in active Class four disease. Full house plus loops is active proliferative disease.
steps.tx: Immunofluorescence microscopy characteristically reveals the **full-house pattern**: dense granular deposition of **IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q** in mesangium and capillary loops, accompanied by prominent **subendothelial** immune complex deposits (**wire-loop lesions**) in active **Class IV** disease. Full house plus loops is active proliferative disease.

vis.alt: Glomerulus with wire loop lesions, subendothelial deposits and mesangial proliferation in lupus nephritis.
vis.caption: Wire loops and subendothelial deposits. The full-house list is in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: First-line induction therapy for active Class three and four proliferative lupus nephritis is glucocorticoids plus either mycophenolate mofetil at a target dose of two to three grams daily or low-dose intravenous cyclophosphamide by the Euro-Lupus regimen: five hundred milligrams every two weeks for six doses, three grams total. Both arms have equivalent renal remission rates. Fertility, bladder and access decide the pick.
steps.tx: First-line **induction** therapy for active Class III and IV proliferative lupus nephritis combines glucocorticoids with either **mycophenolate mofetil** (MMF, target dose **2 to 3 g daily**) or low-dose intravenous **cyclophosphamide** (**Euro-Lupus** regimen: **500 mg** every **2 weeks** for **6 doses**, total **3 g**), both demonstrating equivalent renal remission rates. Pick by fertility, bladder and access.

rows: Target 2 to 3 g daily plus steroids
500 mg every 2 weeks times 6, total 3 g

steps.say: Triple immunosuppressive therapy called multitarget therapy combining mycophenolate mofetil, a calcineurin inhibitor such as tacrolimus two to four milligrams daily or voclosporin, and low-dose glucocorticoids produces significantly higher and faster complete renal response rates in proliferative and mixed Class three and four plus five lupus nephritis. Three prongs are better than two in hard kidneys.
steps.tx: **Triple** immunosuppressive therapy (**multitarget therapy**) combining mycophenolate mofetil, a **calcineurin inhibitor** (**tacrolimus 2 to 4 mg daily** or **voclosporin**), and low-dose glucocorticoids produces significantly higher and faster complete renal response rates in proliferative and mixed Class III/IV plus V lupus nephritis. Three prongs are better than two in hard kidneys.

rows: Tacrolimus 2 to 4 mg daily or voclosporin
Higher faster complete response in III/IV plus V

steps.say: Belimumab, a recombinant human monoclonal antibody against soluble BAFF also called BLyS, is approved for active lupus nephritis based on the BLISS-LN trial. When added to standard-of-care induction with MMF or Euro-Lupus, belimumab significantly improves Primary Efficacy Renal Response and reduces renal flares. B-cell help blockade deepens wins.
steps.tx: **Belimumab**, a recombinant human monoclonal antibody against soluble **BAFF** (BLyS), is approved for active lupus nephritis based on the **BLISS-LN** trial. When added to standard-of-care induction (**MMF** or Euro-Lupus), belimumab significantly improves **Primary Efficacy Renal Response** and reduces renal flares. B-cell help blockade deepens wins.

rows: Primary renal response up, flares down

steps.say: Maintenance therapy for lupus nephritis follows successful induction. Mycophenolate mofetil at one to two grams daily or azathioprine at two milligrams per kilo daily is continued for at least three to five years before considering very gradual, cautious drug withdrawal, alongside indefinite background hydroxychloroquine. Years, not months, are what guard kidneys.
steps.tx: **Maintenance** therapy follows successful induction. **Mycophenolate mofetil** (**1 to 2 g daily**) or **azathioprine** (**2 mg/kg daily**) is continued for at least **3 to 5 years** before considering very gradual, cautious drug withdrawal, alongside indefinite background **hydroxychloroquine**. Years, not months, are what guard kidneys.

rows: At least 3 to 5 years, then feather-slow withdrawal

steps.say: Background supportive care is mandatory in all lupus nephritis patients. Hydroxychloroquine up to five milligrams per kilo actual body weight reduces renal flares, protects against thrombotic events, and improves survival. ACE inhibitors or ARBs target proteinuria reduction and strict blood pressure control below one hundred twenty systolic per KDIGO guidance. Support drugs save lives too.
steps.tx: Background **supportive care** is mandatory in all lupus nephritis patients. **Hydroxychloroquine** (up to **5 mg/kg** actual body weight) reduces renal flares, protects against thrombotic events, and improves survival. **ACE inhibitors or ARBs** target proteinuria reduction and strict blood pressure control (**<120 mmHg systolic** per KDIGO 2024). Support drugs save lives too.

rows: Up to 5 mg/kg, fewer flares and clots, better survival
